draft.title: The lithosphere
card: The lithosphere is the solid outer shell of the Earth. It is made of the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle, the thick layer of hot rock beneath the crust.
The crust is the thin top layer. It forms the continents and the ocean floor, so the lithosphere lies under the oceans as well as on land.
The lithosphere supplies the rocks, minerals and soil parent material that make up the surface. Its landforms include mountains, plains, valleys and volcanoes.
The lithosphere is broken into large pieces called tectonic plates. Their slow movement can build mountains and cause volcanoes and earthquakes.
draft.remember: The lithosphere is the solid rock shell: the crust plus the upper mantle.

a.q: Which of these is part of the lithosphere?
opts: The rock that forms the floor of the Pacific Ocean
The water held in the Great Artesian Basin
The gases that make up the air above Uluru
The kangaroos and plants living near Uluru
a.why: The ocean floor is crust, and crust belongs to the lithosphere. The water in the basin is tempting because it is underground, but it is water, not rock or landform.
a.clue: Look for the option made of solid rock.

b.q: Geologists in Iceland study a volcano that formed where two tectonic plates are moving apart. Why is the volcano part of the lithosphere?
opts: It is a landform built from rock of the crust
It is a place where living things have settled
It is a hot place that warms the air around it
It is a place where ice and water collect
b.why: A volcano is a landform made of rock from the crust and upper mantle, so it belongs to the lithosphere. Plants may grow on it, but living things are not what makes it part of the lithosphere.
b.clue: Think about what the volcano itself is made of.

a.best: The rock that forms the floor of the Pacific Ocean

b.best: It is a landform built from rock of the crust
